item.title: Version 2.12.1
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.12.1 — pinned fan readings and honest units
A fixes-only release: no new panels and no new readings, just three fixes. One of them you will notice every time the battery panel is open; the other two are numbers that were printing units their own tables forbid. A patch number rather than a minor one, because that is what the contents are — the `-SNAPSHOT` in the repo names the next *planned* release, not a commitment, and 2.13.0 stays reserved for the next one that actually adds something.
- **Fixed: the live fan readings scrolled out of sight.** The 🌀 Fans rows were simply the first thing inside the battery panel's scrolling content, so once the panel was tall enough to scroll, reading the Battery, Power, iPhone or Android sections below pushed them off the top of the window. The fans are a property of the Mac rather than of its battery, and they are one of the two bands that move every second — the ⚡ Power rails tick at the same 1 Hz and still scroll with everything else — so they are the band worth keeping in view while reading the rest. They now sit above the scroll area, the way the menu-bar settings and Refresh/Quit footer is pinned below it, and they close with a divider the way the footer opens with one. Two consequences worth naming: the band takes its height out of the scrolling area, so there is a little less room to scroll in exchange for the readings staying in view; and the gap between the fan rows and the 🔋 Battery header is now a divider plus the scroll content's own padding, so it reads a little wider than the old 12pt. Fanless Macs — a MacBook Air — are untouched: no rows, no divider, no reserved space, and the battery header sits flush with the top edge exactly as before.
- **Fixed: sizes and rates could print a figure their own unit rules out.** Three formatters picked the unit from the raw value and then rounded inside that unit, so the top of every band rounded straight past the band. A process between 1023.5 MiB and a gibibyte — including one byte short of it — read "1024 MB" in the RAM panel's per-process list, from a branch that is defined to stop below a gibibyte. 999,950 bytes read "1000.0 KB" in the network session totals, the same figure read "1000.0 KB/s" as a rate in the overview panel's Network row, and 999.6 B/s read "1000 B/s" in the big Download/Upload header — in tables whose next unit begins at 1000. Those now read "1.00 GB", "1.0 MB", "1.0 MB/s" and "1 KB/s". Each window is only half of the last digit actually printed wide, which is why this went unnoticed for so long — but the Download/Upload header draws the value and the unit as separate elements, and it was the one place where a plain "1000" appeared next to a unit that cannot hold it. In the same pass the battery time-remaining formatter picked up the clamp its sibling has always had, so a negative estimate from IOKit can no longer print a figure carrying the sign twice; both call sites already filter those out, so that one is defence for the next caller rather than a reading you have seen.
- **Fixed: on a chip that lays its thermal sensors out differently, the CPU temperature could average a fraction of the die.** Apple Silicon publishes three redundant readings per thermal zone, about 9 °C apart, and StatsBar keeps one of the three. The filter doing that thinning was trusted even when it matched only part of the family, so a chip that instead publishes one sensor per zone — Tp00…Tp07 for eight zones — had six of its eight sensors silently dropped: the CPU temperature became an average over two of them, and only two of the eight cells in the CORES grid carried a temperature at all. It printed a perfectly plausible °C, so nothing downstream could notice. The layout is checked now, and the check is made **per zone** rather than over the whole family — which matters more than it sounds, because the first attempt at this fix judged the family as one unit, and that meant a single anomaly anywhere in it disabled the thinning for every zone. One stray sensor name, or one key missing from a sensor enumeration that skips anything it fails to read, was enough to turn a correct ten-zone reading into an average over all thirty — the same 9 °C error, arriving by the route the fix was written to close, and latched for the whole session because the key list is built once at launch. An anomaly now costs its own zone and nothing else. Being straight about the scope: on the Mac this was measured on, the output is unchanged — the same ten zone keys out of thirty, in the same order — so this is a guard against hardware that has not been observed in the wild rather than a fix for a reading you have seen. Alongside it, a Tp family whose names cannot be decoded now sends the reader to the classic Intel TC** keys instead of handing the per-second read loop keys that fail on every tick.
- **Fixed: release notes were published where nobody could read them.** Every release from 2.6.0 onwards embedded its notes in the update feed in a field this app deliberately does not render, and offered no link to them — so the Changelog button in the update window was hidden, and the notes you are reading are the first in seven releases that the in-app updater can actually open. If you took an update in that range and wondered what changed, that is why.
Most of this release is invisible. The arithmetic behind the memory buckets, the CPU load split, network throughput, hot-battery alert hysteresis, the attached-device bookkeeping, the size and rate formatters and the SMC temperature-key selection now lives in a pure layer with 104 unit tests across seven suites over it; every push to main and every pull request runs that suite and separately compiles, links, signs and verifies the whole app; building a DMG refuses to package a suite that is red or empty; and the steps that publish a release now check themselves — the version, the signature, the signing key, the download URL and the feed's own syntax — instead of relying on whoever is running them. None of that changes anything on screen; the previous implementations were replayed against the new ones, on live readings and on hundreds of thousands of generated ticks, to confirm exactly that. It is the reason the fixes above could be pinned down instead of eyeballed.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (on macOS 15+ the confirmation moved to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ "Open Anyway"), or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`._

item.title: Version 2.12.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.12.0 — per-core detail, fan context, and Free memory told the truth
- **Every logical core now has its own usage bar, with its die temperature above it.** Two cluster averages could never tell one pegged core apart from every core running at a third. One caveat worth knowing: the die publishes more thermal zones than the chip has live cores — ten against eight on a binned M1 Pro — and nothing in the SMC says which zone belongs to which core, so a cell may be showing a neighbour's reading. The spread between cores is only about 3 °C, and the caption names the zone count and the hottest zone so the number that actually matters isn't hidden.
- **Fans now say how hard they are working, not just how fast they are spinning.** 2334 rpm means nothing on its own. Each fan shows its own floor and ceiling and where it currently sits between them, coloured by effort, and a spin-up appears before it becomes audible.
- **Battery cycle count is shown against the pack's rated life** — "307 / 1000 (31%)" instead of a bare 307 that means nothing without the rating.
- **The CPU panel gained thermal pressure, Low Power Mode and load average.** macOS pushes the first two rather than being polled for them, so they cost nothing while the machine is cool and idle. Low Power Mode additionally backs the background sampler off from 2 s to 5 s — a stats app should take that hint rather than work against it. The load average is divided by the core count and labelled as such, so 1.00 means "exactly as much runnable work as this machine has cores".
- **Attached displays are listed:** name, the resolution System Settings shows, the panel's real pixel grid beneath it, refresh rate and diagonal.
- **Values in the panels can be selected and copied.** Serial numbers, MAC and IP addresses, DNS resolvers — the things you open a hardware inspector in order to paste somewhere else — were all dead pixels. Right-click any value for Copy, and right-click a process in the CPU or RAM list to quit it.
- **Fixed: Free memory over-reported by gigabytes.** Cached files — file data the kernel holds on to but can drop the moment something needs the space — were being counted as free. On a 16 GB machine that was 3.2 GB in the wrong column. The bar and legend now carry a Cached Files bucket; the menu-bar percentage is unchanged, because those pages were never counted as used.
- **Fixed: the hot-battery notification did nothing when you clicked it.** It now brings StatsBar forward, where the device that triggered it can be looked at. Two related fixes: the fallback alert played a sound with no setting anywhere to stop it (there is a toggle now, beside the alert switch it belongs to), and on a multi-display desk it could appear over whichever screen happened to have focus instead of beside the menu bar.
- **Fixed: the build did not pin a deployment target,** which silently switched off the compiler's availability checking — a macOS 14-only API would compile without so much as a warning and then crash at runtime on macOS 13. The floor is now declared explicitly and matches what the app says it supports.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.11.1
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.11.1 — crash fix
A patch release for one serious bug: **toggling any menu-bar item in the Control Center crashed the app.**
- **Fixed: the app crashed when you switched a menu-bar item on or off.** Flipping Battery, CPU, RAM, Network or Bluetooth in the Control Center could kill the app outright. Writing the toggle's setting posted a preferences-change notification, whose handler assigned `NSStatusItem.isVisible`; AppKit persists the item's position when you do that, which posted the same notification again — an unbounded recursion that exhausted the main thread's stack. The refresh path now guards against re-entry and only writes `isVisible` on a real change. Present since v2.10.0. - **Fixed: a below-zero battery temperature read as a wildly large positive number.** IOKit reports negative values in the Temperature key as unsigned two's complement, so −5 °C came through as 42,949,667.96 °C — which also made the temperature alert fire about an overheating battery on a freezing one. Positive readings were never affected.
The unconditional `isVisible` write also meant every visible item rewrote a preference once a second; that write is gone, so an idle menu bar now touches user defaults not at all.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.11.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.11.0 — VoiceOver labels and concurrency hardening
- **The menu-bar items are readable by VoiceOver now.** Each one announces what its glyph is showing — "CPU 34%", "Battery 82%, charging", "Network up 1.2 MB/s, down 340 KB/s" — instead of being an unlabelled button. The label is refreshed only when the value actually changes, so an idle menu bar costs nothing extra. - **Thread-safety hardening across every reader.** The readers are now compiler-enforced main-thread types, and the iPhone/Android USB enumeration runs in dedicated worker actors that own their own caches. Nothing changes on screen; it removes a class of latent data races around the device caches, which were previously kept safe only by convention. - **Correct memory figures under translation.** The RAM buckets are now sized with the kernel page size rather than the process page size. Identical on native Apple Silicon and Intel Macs — it only differed for a translated process, where every bucket read four times too small. - The bundled `cocobat.py` CLI bounds its subprocess calls with a timeout instead of hanging indefinitely on a wedged `ioreg` or libimobiledevice call.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.10.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.10.0 — Reliability fixes across CPU, Network, Bluetooth, and Android
- **CPU usage no longer freezes on long uptimes:** fixed a Mach host-port leak in the CPU reader that, after a day or two of continuous running, could make the CPU readout stop updating until the app was restarted. - **Bluetooth accessory battery recovers after an off→on toggle:** the battery level of BLE accessories (e.g. a Logitech mouse) no longer sticks at its last value after you turn Bluetooth off and back on — it reconnects and resumes live updates. - **Menu-bar network rate clears on disconnect:** the throughput shown in the menu bar now drops to 0 when the connection goes away, instead of freezing at the last value while the popover already says "No active network connection". - **Intel Macs now show CPU temperature:** the classic Intel die-temperature sensors are decoded correctly (they were silently rejected before, leaving the reading blank). - **Android battery: faster reads and refresh on reconnect:** the learned battery capacity is re-read when you replug a phone, and the capacity read now filters on-device instead of transferring the multi-MB battery-history dump. - **Bluetooth device list refreshes at the intended rate:** it was updating roughly half as often as intended while the popover was open. - **Housekeeping:** de-duplicated popover components (CPU/Memory legends, the show-more toggles) and removed dead code.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.9.1
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.9.1
- **More frequent update checks:** the background update check now runs every 6 hours instead of once a day, so new versions arrive sooner. You can still trigger a check any time from the "Check for updates…" button.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.9.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.9.0
Even less background work, plus a batch of robustness fixes.
- **iPhone/iPad:** the menu-bar battery glyph now uses a lightweight read, while the heavier diagnostics read (temperature and detailed battery) runs only while the popover is open — so fewer helper processes fire when a phone is connected but you're not looking at it. Hot-battery alerts stay as responsive as before. - **Battery:** macOS's "Maximum Capacity" health figure is fetched only while the battery popover is open (it's a detail-only number), so the periodic `system_profiler` call no longer runs in the background. - **Updates:** information-only Sparkle updates now open their info page instead of offering a broken download, and a mid-download content-length change no longer skews the progress bar. - **Under the hood:** background-read timing is now on a monotonic clock (immune to system clock changes), the network-interface MAC read avoids undefined pointer access, the DNS server list renders stably when addresses repeat, and the public-IP lookup tidies up its per-fetch network session.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.8.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.8.0
Less work when you're not looking.
- **Menu-bar toggles now cut real work:** turning a metric off (Battery / CPU / RAM / Network) actually stops its background reader instead of just hiding the icon — so hiding what you don't use lowers CPU and energy. It resumes the instant you turn it back on or open the popover. - **Lower idle usage:** each menu-bar icon is redrawn only when its value changes (and never while hidden); the battery reads back off to a lazy poll — refreshed immediately on plug/unplug via a power-source notification — and the network reader stops entirely when its rate isn't on screen. - **iPhone/iPad:** far fewer background helper processes when a phone is connected but nothing is showing it, and the device's name/model are cached instead of re-read every second. - **Under the hood:** the battery and CPU sensor readers now share a single SMC connection.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.7.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.7.0
More performance and reach.
- **Network:** latency and reachability now work on IPv6-only connections. Previously the ping was IPv4-only, so an IPv6-only link showed the internet as unreachable with no latency even when it was fine. - **Lower idle usage:** iPhone/iPad and Android battery polling now backs off to a slow keep-warm when neither the popover nor the phone menu-bar item is showing — no more shelling out to libimobiledevice/adb every second for a phone nothing is watching. (Hot-battery alerts for a connected iPhone stay as responsive as before.) - **Under the hood:** the readers' background-read throttling is unified into one helper, and the SMC sensor reads skip a redundant syscall per key.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._

item.title: Version 2.6.0
item.description:
# StatsBar v2.6.0
Performance and polish.
- **Android (multi-device):** fixed battery health being dropped or misreported when more than one Android phone is connected — each device's state is now tracked independently. - **CPU:** the frequency readout no longer shows a wrong value for one tick right after reopening the popover. - **Lower idle usage:** battery power-rail/fan SMC reads and iPhone/iPad USB polling now back off while their panel is closed, cutting background work. - **UI:** the Android "show more" expand no longer stutters; removed a duplicate "Status" row in the Network panel.
_Not notarized — right-click → Open on first launch (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/StatsBar.app`)._
